_doc: CANONICAL cross-repo acceptance vectors for the suppression contract.
THE INVARIANT THESE ENCODE:
ANY authoritative plane says DO NOT CONTACT  =>  governed prospect send REFUSES,
evaluated at send time, at the irreversible boundary.
- positive suppression on any trusted leg            -> BLOCK
- negative permission (clear to send) is valid ONLY when ALL required
legs were successfully consulted
- a required leg unreadable -> UNKNOWN -> an automated prospect send
REFUSES. An unreadable authority NEVER becomes CLEAR.
WHY THIS FILE IS SHARED. Three planes can mail a prospect: clawd governed
Gmail, modex governed Gmail, and the war-room SendGrid coverage lane. One
sales system cannot hold three definitions of 'do not contact'. This file is
copied verbatim into all three repos and each repo's suite pins its SHA-256,
so a copy that drifts turns that repo RED instead of quietly disagreeing.
A suppression key that differs between the asking plane and the answering
plane is worse than no key at all: it reports CLEAR with total confidence.
EVERY VECTOR ASSERTS A SPECIFIC REASON, never merely that something was
blocked. `assert reason == 'modex_do_not_contact'` and not `assert blocked`.
A suite of positive cases alone would pass against `() => 'blocked'`.
PROVENANCE: measured 2026-08-16 against the real stores. 242 of 1,936 modex
personas carry do_not_contact=TRUE; 204 are absent from clawd suppression;
146 of those are targetable by clawd today; 1 was already mailed at that
exact address. S1 and S2 are the two confirmed fires, not inventions.
_key_vectors_doc: The block_key pairs, pinned here so the TypeScript and Python mirrors are
held to ONE definition of who a person is. This is the highest-stakes
drift in the estate: if the ASKING plane and the ANSWERING plane key
differently, the answering plane replies 'no suppression matched' with
total confidence, and that is indistinguishable from consent.
`siblings` MUST produce the same key. `different_people` MUST NOT.
The controls are not padding: a first pass keyed on any shared name token
reported 88 sibling pairs where 7 survive inspection.

vectors.name: EXACT do-not-contact recorded in modex
vectors.why: seannewtz@dswinc.com is do_not_contact=TRUE in modex AND appears in clawd's outreach_sends at that EXACT address. Not an alias miss, not a dedup miss: a straight override of a decision we recorded and could see.

vectors.name: SIBLING address, blocked via the coarse block_key
vectors.why: modex holds john.drake@homedepot.com as do_not_contact; clawd mailed john_d_drake@homedepot.com. Both a visibility failure AND a person-resolution failure. Exact-match suppression cannot catch this.

vectors.name: FALSE-SIBLING CONTROL, two humans sharing one token
vectors.why: A first pass keyed on ANY shared name token reported 88 'siblings'; at a large employer one shared token is just a common first name. brian.watson and brian.guinn are different people and a suppression on one must NOT silently suppress the other. This control is why the key requires the full surviving token set.

vectors.name: modex leg UNREADABLE on an automated prospect send
vectors.why: The whole point of the contract. An authority we cannot read is UNKNOWN, and UNKNOWN is not CLEAR. Turning an unreachable store into permission is how a halt stays falsely LIVE.

vectors.name: clawd suppression TRUE, modex candidate
vectors.why: The mirror of S1. clawd's do_not_send is authoritative for every plane, not only for clawd's own Gmail. Direction of visibility must not decide whether a decision counts.

vectors.name: SendGrid global/unsubscribe suppression TRUE
vectors.why: The recipient's OWN act, and the only leg that is legally binding rather than an inference we maintain about them. It currently reaches clawd through a nightly cron sync that silently no-ops without an API key, which means yesterday's unsubscribe is invisible to today's send. It must be a read, not a sync.

vectors.name: ALL required legs CLEAR and a strict authorize identity is valid
vectors.why: The contract must be able to say YES, or it is a kill switch rather than a gate. This is the only vector that proceeds, and it proceeds to the DOWNSTREAM guards (autonomy, caps, dedup) rather than to the wire.

vectors.name: coarse block_key MATCHES but strict authorize_key does NOT
vectors.why: THE ASYMMETRY, stated as a test. A strict identity mismatch must never RESCUE a coarse block. The keys are not two opinions to be reconciled: block_key governs refusal and authorize_key governs permission, and permission cannot overturn a refusal. If this ever goes green by allowing, someone has wired authorize_key into the blocking path.

vectors.name: strict authorize identity EXISTS but a suppression leg is positive
vectors.why: S8's sibling on the other axis. A perfectly resolved HubSpot identity is an answer to 'who is this', never to 'may we mail them'. A resolved person who opted out is a resolved person who opted out.

vectors.name: VERBAL do-not-call blocks EMAIL
vectors.why: A human said 'do not contact me' out loud on a call. Today that blocks the SendGrid lane and not Gmail, so the same person is protected on one plane and cold-emailed from another. LEAD ruled 2026-08-16 that it blocks email: a false block is recoverable and invisible to the buyer, a false allow is neither, and honouring it on Gmail is a TIGHTENING on one plane rather than a loosening on any. Recorded as a reversible default.

vectors.name: HubSpot leg UNREADABLE on an automated prospect send
vectors.why: S4 for the leg LEAD made required on 2026-08-16. HubSpot is the only authority all three planes already write to, and it is the recipient's own act rather than our inference. Unreadable is UNKNOWN, never CLEAR.

vectors.name: an unkeyable candidate address is UNKNOWN, not CLEAR
vectors.why: block_key returns null for input it cannot key. A leg cannot answer a question about a person it cannot identify, so 'no suppression row matched' is not evidence of consent here. The empty-string case is the one an operator hits with a malformed import.
